newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovakia forecasts GDP growth at 5.8 pct in 2000.
newsitem.headline: Slovakia forecasts GDP growth at 5.8 pct in 2000.

text.p: Slovak real annual gross domestic product (GDP) growth is forecast to slow to 5.8 percent through 2000 from 6.4 percent growth in 1996, the Slovak government said on Tuesday.

"Based on the economy's previous developments, GDP is expected to grow at a 6.0-6.2 percent pace in the 1996-1997 period and then moderate further through the year 2000," an official government report obtained by Reuters said.
The document, the Update of Financial Strategy for the 1997-2000 Period, gave a series of macroeconomic forcasts, but did not suggest specific measures to help obtain them.

"The share of household consumption on GDP will only slightly increase, the share of state administration consumption slightly decline, while fixed capital creation will rise significantly," the document said.
Slovakia's first half GDP in 1996 was robust at 7.1 percent, compared with 6.1 percent in 1995, and was boosted mainly by domestic consumption.
The document said the average year-on-year inflation rate is estimated at 6.0 percent in 1996, 6.2 percent in 1997, 6.0 percent in 1998 and 5.9 percent through 2000.
The average inflation rate in the first half of the year was 6.2 percent, after 9.9 percent in the whole year of 1995.
The average unemployment rate is expected gradually to fall to 12.1 percent in 1996, 11.3 percent in 1997, 10.6 percent in 1998, 9.9 percent in 1999 and 9.3 percent in 2000.

The first half average unemployment rate hit 13 percent on the total workforce after 13.8 percent in 1995. The state budget deficit is expected to account for 4.1 percent of GDP in 1996, 3.2 percent in 1997, 2.5 percent in 1998, 1.8 percent in 1999, and 1.0 percent in 2000. Officially, the state budget deficit in the first-half of 1996 accounted for 2.2 percent of GDP after totalling 1.6 percent of GDP for the whole of last year.
